title: Open-source decision models: the decision sets in three formats, a model answering through the same interface, compared on dev
request: Export the decision datasets in each family's format from one builder (tabular, chat with a dataset card, typed questions), write fine-tuning recipes for a small open-source model, register the tuned model as an answerer and compare it with the classifiers and the rules; used only where it passes.
spec: One builder in dclab_core, a writer for the generated sets, a gateway purpose and an answerer class for a model, a comparison harness that never spends without a cap, and a fine-tuning recipe; the run is the owner's.
plan: Survey the decision sets, the gateway, the prompts and the existing LoRA script.
Write the three exports from the same rows, sealed rows never written.
Add the decision_answer purpose, its prompt and a model answerer; compare a local model on dev.
Review, plant faults, fix, measure again.

decisions.decision: A model is asked exactly as the chat export trains it: one request builder for both.
decisions.why: A tuned model compared on inputs it never saw measures the mismatch, not the model.

decisions.decision: The chat export's answer is the label alone, with no reason.
decisions.why: A reason learned from invented tables would be said about real columns.

decisions.decision: The comparison refuses a fallback to another tier and a remote model without a cap.
decisions.why: A tuned tier that cannot answer would silently be replaced by a paid one.

decisions.decision: The fine-tuning run, and the sealed verdict, are left open and said so.
decisions.why: The GPU and the model are the owner's decision, and every sealed set of v1 was already read.

change: dclab_core/decision_export.py (new), answerers.py (ModelAnswerer), prompts/decision_answer.md (dclab-core 0.30.0), dclab_rnd/decision_export.py (new; make decisions-export), decision_model_compare.py (new), models/settings.py (the decision_answer purpose), agents/harness.py, decisions/finetune/README.md, .gitignore; tests/test_decision_export.py (new), test_model_data_limits.py; evidence decision_llm_v1; the plan, the roadmap, CLAUDE.md.

findings.defect: The local model's long replies stopped the comparison.
findings.scenario: A reply cut at the token limit raised in the middle of the run.
findings.cause: The advisor treats a cut reply as a failure, and the answerer let it propagate.
findings.fix: A failed request is an abstention, counted; the answer may use 300 tokens.

findings.defect: Removing the check that the purpose is served by the tier asked for went unnoticed.
findings.scenario: A planted fault dropped the check and every test passed.
findings.cause: The earlier refusals stopped every tested case first.
findings.fix: A test where the tuned tier cannot answer and the gateway would fall back.

findings.defect: The tuned comparison could spend money and record a paid model as local.
findings.scenario: With no tuned tier set and an API key present, the purpose fell back to the cheap tier on a paid endpoint, recorded as tuned and local.
findings.cause: The local check was skipped for the tuned path and the record hard-coded local.
findings.fix: The tuned tier must be set; a remote one needs a cap; the purpose must be served by the tier asked for; local is read from the tier.

findings.defect: A tuned model would be trained on one input and asked another.
findings.scenario: The chat export held a prose question under its own system text; the answerer sent JSON under the prompt file.
findings.cause: Two builders for the same request.
findings.fix: One request builder; the chat export holds the prompt file and the same JSON the model is sent.

findings.defect: The training answers taught a false reason.
findings.scenario: Every answer ended with a reason saying the column was planted in an invented table, which a tuned model would repeat about real columns.
findings.cause: A reason written from the label's source.
findings.fix: The answer is the label alone.

findings.defect: A JSON true or false answer was discarded.
findings.scenario: A reply with answer true matched neither yes nor no and counted as an abstention.
findings.cause: The answer was matched as text.
findings.fix: A JSON boolean is read as yes or no; the typed export writes the answer as one of the options.

findings.defect: The recipe promised a sealed gate that cannot run.
findings.scenario: Every sealed set of v1 was read in 22.3 and the gate runner takes fitted classifiers only.
findings.fix: The recipe and the status say a sealed verdict needs a new generated set and a runner for any answerer: open.

findings.defect: The local run could ask a different model than the one it recorded.
findings.scenario: An intern model setting took precedence over the model named on the command line.
findings.cause: The tier's model reads that setting first.
findings.fix: The setting is cleared and the model is named for the purpose.

findings.defect: The table export carried whole column and target names.
findings.scenario: Two columns held the names where only their tokens should be.
findings.cause: Every state field was a column.
findings.fix: Whole names are left out; their tokens stay.

findings.defect: The answerer could send states its purpose does not describe.
findings.scenario: A project or workflow decision's state holds measures and codes the purpose's limit does not name.
findings.fix: A model answers column decisions only; another point is refused.

measurements.name: a local model beside the rules and the classifiers on 240 dev decisions
measurements.gate: the comparison recorded on the same decisions: coverage, agreement with the rule and accuracy against the benchmark labels
measurements.result: the rules right on 0.9333; the classifiers 0.875 to 1.0 on their points' 40; a local Qwen 2.5 coder 1.5B, not tuned, 0.4507 on the 213 it answered (0.4 of all), 23 failed requests
measurements.against_gate: recorded for every answerer on the same 240 decisions
limits: A small base model, not the tuned one the package asks for.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each planted fault fails a test
measurements.result: 8 of 8 planted faults caught after the tests were strengthened

outcome: The decision sets export in three formats from the same records, a model answers through the same interface as the rules exactly as it would be trained, and its comparison is recorded; the fine-tuning run and a sealed verdict wait for the owner's GPU and a new generated set.
lessons: Train and ask a model through one function, or the comparison measures the difference between them.
Never teach a model a reason that is only true of the training data.
A measurement that must not spend checks the tier that will answer, not the one it asked for.
risks: A sealed verdict for a model needs a new generated set.
